subject: Reserved pool rate guarantee — renewal expansion terms
messages:
From: Ellen Park <ellen@cloudwave.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: Cloudwave Procurement <procure@cloudwave.com>
Date: Sat, 01 Aug 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal questions — need guaranteed token/sec for Q4 burst

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks for the walkthrough last week. We’re preparing our renewal approval packet and the procurement team has asked for a clear throughput guarantee for the reserved pool if we increase our committed GPUs. Specifically: during our Q4 marketing surge we expect sustained bursts to ~1.8M tokens/hour (~500 tokens/sec) for up to 6 hours/day over 4 weeks.

Can Redwood provide a tokens/sec SLO for the new reserved pool ( +8 A100-equivalent GPUs ), and outline failure/fallback behavior if we exceed the SLO? Also procurement wants language around measurement windows, credits calculation, and any uplift pricing for burst capacity.

We’re on a tight timeline — procurement will need final SLA language by Aug 6 to make the payment cycle for a Sept 1 renewal effective date.

Best,
Ellen
Ellen Park
Head of Platform Ops
Cloudwave Inc
ellen@cloudwave.com

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Ellen Park <ellen@cloudwave.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 03 Aug 2026 09:24:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal questions — need guaranteed token/sec for Q4 burst

Hi Ellen — thanks for the clear numbers and timeline. We can support the +8 A100-equivalent reserved pool expansion and propose the following high-level SLOs for the addendum:

- Guaranteed throughput: 500 tokens/sec sustained per reserved pool for up to 6 continuous hours/day, measured as a 5-minute rolling average, with coverage window 00:00–23:59 UTC for the contracted period.
- Capacity buffer: automatic soft-burst of up to 30% above guaranteed throughput for short spikes (<30s) with no additional charge; sustained bursts beyond buffer subject to burst pricing.
- Measurement & credits: SLO measured per UTC day; if monthly availability of guaranteed throughput <99.5% (measured as total seconds below guarantee / total contract seconds), Customer receives a pro-rata credit equal to 10% of monthly committed pool fee per 0.5% shortfall, capped at 50% of monthly committed fee.
- Failure/fallback behavior: automatic routing to compatible model variants in other pools/regions if local pool unavailable; best-effort latency for fallback with no additional SLA credit beyond the throughput credit above.

I’m attaching a draft addendum and a throughput calculation workbook so procurement can validate the credit math. Rafael and Marissa — can you review the draft SLO language and confirm the credit calculation table? We tried to balance customer protection with predictable economics for Redwood.

Next steps: if this looks acceptable I can put the addendum into DocuSign and loop in procurement for signature before Aug 6.

Thanks,
Stephanie
Steph Nguyen
Strategic Accounts — Renewals
Redwood Inference
stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com
Attachment: redwood-cloudwave-sla-draft.pdf (PDF), throughput-calculation-sheet.xlsx (XLSX)

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>, Ellen Park <ellen@cloudwave.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 04 Aug 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal questions — need guaranteed token/sec for Q4 burst

Ellen/Steph — reviewed the draft. A few legal/ops clarifications we should add before we finalize:

- Define "tokens/sec" measurement tie-in: we should explicitly reference Redwood API token definitions (prompt + completion tokens) and the measurement point (ingress at the serving gateway).
- Include a remediation window: Redwood will provide a 72-hour remediation period after detection of an SLO breach to attempt corrective action before the credit applies; the clock for remediation begins at detection time logged in our incident-tracking system.
- Force majeure & region outage carveouts: if the shortfall is due to region-wide capacity exhaustion caused by third-party cloud provider events, credits should not apply; instead we provide documented mitigation steps and prioritized capacity re-assignment.
- Audit rights: Cloudwave may request throughput measurement logs for the disputed period; propose a request-once-per-year audit right with a mutually agreed data-redaction process and cost-share for extensive audits.

If procurement agrees to these, I can add the clauses into section 3 of the addendum. Also note that the credit calculation in the workbook assumes pro-rata monthly billing; Marissa — please confirm pricing bands for sustained burst >30% so we can include explicit uplift rates.

-Rafael
Rafael Mendes
Senior Counsel, Commercial
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Renewal questions — need guaranteed token/sec for Q4 burst

Thanks — this is very helpful and close to what procurement needs. A few quick items from procurement:

- Measurement point language is fine as long as we get the raw daily throughput logs for any invoked credit. We accept the once-per-year audit with cost-share.
- The 72-hour remediation window is acceptable, but we’d like an SLA escalation path in writing (named contacts + escalation timeline) so Cloudwave can follow up during an incident.
- For region outage carveouts, can Redwood add a secondary option for ephemeral capacity from your Dedicated burst pool with pre-agreed uplift rates? Procurement wants a documented fallback that doesn’t rely solely on cross-region routing.

If you can add those three bullets to the addendum and send the updated PDF + DocuSign link, procurement will sign and aim for a Sept 1 effective renewal date. Appreciate the fast turnaround.

Ellen

Cloudwave Inc
